correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the complete maximal subgroup list: A itself and, for each maximal index-p hyperplane preimage L<A, the p groups L union (a s)L indexed by a mod L. Since A is abelian and inversion stabilizes L, these are subgroups and are all maximal. Counting hyperplanes of A_p/pA_p yields M=1+sum p h_p and Frattini Phi(G)=product pA_p. Each reflection lies in one extension of each L and has incidence H=sum h_p; a rotation with nonzero Sylow residues at S lies in M-sum_{p in S}p^{r_p} maximal subgroups. Binomial-independent residue counts give the polynomial. The elementary combinatorial identity ui=1+max_{g notin Phi}delta(g) then gives M+1-min p^{r_p}; reflection degree cannot exceed this rotation maximum because their difference is sum_{p != p*}(p^{r_p}-1)>=0. Wrote and executed an independently implemented group-multiplication/subgroup-closure enumeration (not repository program) for A=C2xC2, C3xC3, C4xC2, C2xC3 and C3xC3xC5; exhaustive subgroup lists give expected profiles/maximal counts/ui=4,5,4,5,14 respectively. General theorem follows the all-finite-abelian structural argument, not the samples.

evidence: A generic relation between maximal-subgroup incidence and ui=1+max_{g outside Phi}delta(g) is elementary and not novel.

value.rationale: Maximal subgroup intersection properties are a natural finite-group invariant, with a recent paper computing only cyclic dihedral cases. This result extends to arbitrary abelian kernels including noncyclic p-ranks and even-order kernels, giving the complete elementwise incidence distribution rather than only one threshold. Rank dependence captures genuine structure absent from the cyclic formula; it is an all-family classification rather than a small-instance exercise.

limitations: Nontrivial finite abelian inversion kernel only; includes nonfaithful inversion on even torsion.
Cyclic kernel ui and abstract Frattini incidence concepts preexist.
